Diffraction-ready average R-3m B4C model in the conventional hexagonal setting. The atomic coordinates follow the Clark-Hoard/JCPDS average structure; split B/C occupancy on the polar icosahedral site gives exactly B36C9 in the cell. The lattice parameters a=5.601(1) A and c=12.087(5) A are the ambient sample values reported by Somayazulu et al. in the official supplement and give V=328.383 A^3, consistent with the fixed 328.4 A^3 EOS reference volume. Structure references: Clark and Hoard, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 65, 2115-2119 (1943), doi:10.1021/ja01251a026; Somayazulu et al. (2023), doi:10.1098/rsta.2022.0331; JCPDS/PDF 6-0555. PhaseSmith can expand the five asymmetric sites to calculate powder reflections and intensities.

<summary>Thermal equation choices</summary>

- **Debye temperature law:** integrated\_gruneisen

</details>

BM3 reference isotherm from the room-temperature quench-data fit, held fixed in the P-V-T fit of the Mie-Grüneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The thermal model uses n = 5 atoms per B4C formula unit and is the paper's generalized Tange relation with a = 1. The average disordered R-3m structure is reported stable over the experimental range.

At the official heated data's printed V and T, this pair gives a pressure RMSE of 1.39 GPa and chi-squared per observation of 0.961. A full Peritheos P-V-T errors-in-variables refit with gamma0 fixed gives q=1.050(519), so the refit is documented as a diagnostic rather than promoted over the published pair.

<summary>Thermal equation choices</summary>

- **Thermal expansion law:** linear\_temperature
- **Reference volume law:** berman

</details>

The paper's Berman P-V-T fit, made with the EosFit7c program: V0(T) = V0\*\[1 + alpha0\*(T-Tr) + 0.5\*alpha1\*(T-Tr)^2\] and K0(T) = K0 + dK0/dT\*(T-Tr), with the 300 K BM3 parameters fixed. The authors call this parameterization unphysical and offer it as a ready estimate of K(P, T).

The article displays an exponential-integral formula that instead matches EosFit's Fei-style law. Peritheos stores the actual EosFit Berman curve and documents both fitting objectives.
